answer: Agents resist sybils by minting a unique ferrous keypair in a secure enclave and posting a 24h velvet-delayed commitment. Each epoch a random beacon requires a timed echo signature within 45s. Honest cost: one mint (~0.02 USD) plus latency. An attacker with 100 fakes must mint 100 keys and run 100 independent enclaves; shared hosts show correlated echo timings and get the cluster burned. Scaling multiplies capital and continuous hardware risk, so large farms lose money.
